title: Effects of combined surface treatments of aluminium nanoparticle on its corrosion resistance before and after inclusion into an epoxy coating

nodes.label: Epoxy coatings on steel need both a barrier and an active inhibitor; bare Al nanoparticle fillers corrode and agglomerate
The combined effect of a cerium conversion layer and a silane graft on Al nanoparticles, before and after inclusion in epoxy, is unreported
A Ce oxide/hydroxide film should inhibit the particle actively while grafted APTES should make it organophilic and bond it into the epoxy
Aluminium nanoparticles as the functional filler of a two-component epoxy on mild steel

attrs.reason: Al offers barrier plus sacrificial action

nodes.label: Two-step surface treatment: cerium nitrate / H2O2 conversion, then APTES silane grafting
Modification-bath pH 3.0-4.2, three APTES routes (Si-Al-1/2/3), filler loading 1-3 wt%

attrs.variable: bath pH; silanisation route; filler loading

nodes.label: Cerium conversion layer grown on the Al nanoparticles from 5 mmol/L Ce(NO3)3 + H2O2 at pH 3.8, 10 min
APTES grafted by sol-gel at 60 C reflux, pH adjusted to 8-9
Particles homogenised and sonicated into epoxy, applied on steel and cured 30 min at 120 C
The treated particle surface carries CeO2, Ce2O3 and Ce-OH over aluminium oxide and metallic Al
APTES is chemically grafted through Si-O-Al with free amine ends; Si-Al-2 and Si-Ce-Al carry the most silane
Surface treatment slows nanoparticle corrosion in pH 1: evolved H2 falls from 1.7 mL (Al) to 0.7 mL (Si-Al-2)
Silane-treated particles are more evenly dispersed in the cured epoxy than untreated ones
Coating barrier resistance after 57 d in 3.5% NaCl: S2 and S4 reach ~10^10.5 ohm cm2 against ~10^4.5 for the blank
Wet adhesion loss after salt spray falls from 44% (blank) to 18% for the silane-treated fillers
After 360 h salt spray the S2 and S4 coatings corrode only along the scribe while blank and untreated-filler coatings are destroyed
The dense siloxane shell blocks water at the particle and its amine ends cross-link into the epoxy, removing the void network that carries electrolyte
Cerium conversion plus APTES grafting protects the nanoparticle itself and, through better dispersion and bonding, the whole epoxy coating
Al 2p resolves into two components at 75.4 eV (aluminium oxide) and 78.2 eV (aluminium), the metal component the larger

nodes.label: APTES turns the particle surface from polar to non-polar, so silanised particles settle in the polar solvent
The metastable Ce(III)/Ce(IV) film acts as an active inhibitor, converting under Cl- attack and resisting the alkali generated by the cathodic reaction
Dispersion is judged from one FE-SEM field per coating and the Ce layer is too thin to resolve by FE-SEM or XPS Ce 3d
2 wt% of the combined Ce+silane filler is the optimum; higher loadings re-agglomerate and lose impedance

notes: Two-level spine: the treatment is first validated on the particle (s10/s11 -> s12) and then in the coating (s13 -> s14/s15 -> s16). Audits: a1 (no Ce 3d peak above noise in the survey inset, so the whole Ce-layer composition claim rests on O 1s deconvolution), a2 (the claimed 140 min hydrogen latency is not in the curves), a3 (S vs M adhesion ranking inside the error bars). q2 is marked contradicts: the text calls the cerium-oxide O 1s contribution much weaker than the hydroxide, the panel shows the opposite. Packet figure ids run one behind the paper from F4 on (packet F4 = paper Fig. 5). F7 (hydrogen evolution) is tier C and offers no panel crops, so its two nodes carry panel_ids []. Numbers are read off the panels, not the MatMech block, which credits S4 alone with >10^10 ohm cm2 where the panel puts S2 on the same curve. Lost: FTIR, Tables 3-7, the pH sweep detail of the cerium bath, and the dry pull-off strengths.

changes: q10: provenance derived -> measured. The bars are the paper's Eq. (8) reduction of dry and wet pull-off strengths, but neither strength is an OBS node here, and v04 requires an incoming derives edge for provenance=derived (83/83 derived nodes in r01-r04 have one). The reduction stays visible through k3 premise_for q10 and is now stated in image_note.

q2: image_note replaced with the measured component heights (CeO2 ~100, Ce2O3 ~285, Al-O ~380, Ce-OH ~250), which is what carries image_support=contradicts; also records that the figure labels the 530 eV component 'Ce2O', a figure typo for Ce2O3.

a1: image_note now says the 820-880 eV Ce 3d enlargement lies OUTSIDE the F2a crop and is visible only in the whole-figure image (flat scatter, ~1150-1280 counts, no doublet). A reader given the crop alone cannot check this audit.
q8: image_note sharpened - S2 and S4 overlap at ~10^10.4 at the lowest plotted frequency, and S1's last point drops to ~10^6.0 against a ~10^6.8 plateau.

panel_checks.note: F2c is the O 1s deconvolution and carries exactly the four assignments the node lists. The contradiction is real: Ce2O3 (~285) > Ce-OH (~250) and CeO2+Ce2O3 (~385) dominate it, so image_support=contradicts is right.

F2a is the survey with the dashed Ce 3d circle; the enlargement it points to is flat scatter with no doublet. Panel id is right even though the enlargement is cropped out of panel a - it belongs to panel a's pointer and the store offers no id for it.

F6b (paper Fig. 7b, MEK) plots Al as the reference series alongside Si-Al-1/2/3 and Si-Ce-Al. Al runs 3750 -> 1280 NTU over 60 min; the silanised series start at 1400-2000 and end at 400-600. Numbers and the image_note about differing starting dispersions both check out.
Extra check on F10c. S2 (diamond) and S4 (square) do sit on top of one another at ~10^10.4 at the lowest frequency, S3 ~10^6.9, blank ~10^4.5. The node's flag against the MatMech block is right.
Extra check. F2b resolves Al2O3 at 75.4 eV (~17 counts) and Al at 78.2 eV (~72), the metal component the larger, as stated.

review.audit_summary: 4 audits (a1, a2, a3, lim1) plus q2's contradicts flag, all within budget and each changing support for a named spine claim. The three kinds are kept apart properly: q2 and a2 are figure-contradicts-text (the O 1s intensity ordering; the claimed 140 min hydrogen latency), a1 is figure-does-not-resolve-it (no Ce 3d signal above noise, so the whole s10 composition claim leans on one O 1s deconvolution), and a3 is a within-scatter audit on the S-over-M adhesion ranking. lim1 correctly restates a1 plus the one-field dispersion limit as a method limitation. None overstates: a1 says the layer is below detection, not absent.
